claim: Operant tasks can answer questions about whether an animal's motivation for a specific nutrient has changed.
source: Has their motivation for a specific nutrient changed? Has their feeding gained a compulsive nature that is insensitive to satiety signals? These questions can be answered with operant tasks, where rodents receive food contingent on their actions (Curtis et al., 2019; Mourra et al., 2020; O'Connor et al., 2015; Skinner, 1938; Thorndike, 1898; Wald et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on operant tasks.

claim: Training in dedicated operant chambers can take weeks for animals to learn.
source: Training in dedicated operant chambers has limitations: tasks can take weeks for animals to learn, animals may be tested at different phases of their circadian cycle due to equipment availability, and food restriction can be necessary to get animals to seek food outside of their home-cage, which can confound feeding studies.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of traditional operant training methods.

claim: Testing operant behavior in rodent home-cages results in both fewer interventions from the researcher and faster rates of learning (Balzani et al., 2018; Francis and Kanold, 2017; Lee et al., 2020).
source: To mitigate these issues, several researchers have begun to test operant behavior in rodent home-cages, resulting in both fewer interventions from the researcher and faster rates of learning (Balzani et al., 2018; Francis and Kanold, 2017; Lee et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

evidence: This is a direct statement about the technical specifications of the microcontroller.

claim: The microcontroller contains a battery charging circuit for charging the internal 4400mAhr LiPo battery in FED3.
source: The microcontroller also contains a battery charging circuit for charging the internal 4400mAhr LiPo battery in FED3, which provides ~1 week of run-time between charges.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the battery charging capabilities.

claim: The code for FED3 is written in the Arduino language and is fully open-source.
source: The code for FED3 is written in the Arduino language and is fully open-source.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the programming language and availability of the code.

claim: In FR1 mode, when the mouse activates the left nose-poke, the FED3 delivers a combined auditory tone (4 kHz for 0.3 s) and visual (all eight LEDs light in blue) stimulus and dispenses a pellet.
source: In FR1 mode, FED3 logs the time-stamps of each 'nose-poke' event to the internal storage. When the mouse activates the left nose-poke, the FED3 delivers a combined auditory tone (4 kHz for 0.3 s) and visual (all eight LEDs light in blue) stimulus and dispenses a pellet.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the operation of the FR1 program.

claim: Viral infections of male and female Drd1-Cre mice were conducted under 0.5–2.5% anesthesia on a stereotaxic apparatus.
source: Viral infections of male and female Drd1-Cre mice were conducted under 0.5–2.5% anesthesia on a stereotaxic apparatus.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the surgical procedures used.

claim: 500 nL of AAV2-DIO-hSyn-ChR2 was injected bilaterally (500 nL/hemisphere) in the dorsomedial striatum.
source: Using a Nanoject injector, 500 nL of AAV2-DIO-hSyn-ChR2 was injected bilaterally (500 nL/hemisphere) in the dorsomedial striatum.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the viral injection procedure.

claim: ChR2 was allowed to express for 4 weeks before behavioral testing.
source: After letting ChR2 express for 4 weeks, animals were pre-trained on an FR1 schedule for pellets overnight in their home-cage.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental timeline.

source: During the self-stimulation session, when the mouse poked on the active nose-poke, it received a 1 s train of 1 mW 475 nm light at 20 Hz.
